acceptance: Agent sessions authenticate as the separate identity (gh api user)
A stand-in posted by that identity is rejected by the gate
context:
Owner-only: needs a GitHub App or fine-grained token created by the repository owner.

Revalidated 2026-11-11: still required; blocked on the owner creating the agent identity (GitHub App or fine-grained token) and switching agent `gh auth` to it. Evidence: `gh auth status` and `gh api user` today show login joeharris76 with scopes admin:org, gist, repo, workflow, write:packages; origin/develop .github/review.yml lists attesters [joeharris76]. The description's file reference was updated from the removed STANDIN_ATTESTERS to review.yml. A fine-grained PAT cannot carry admin:org, and the same identity would also let agents run `gh repo delete` (human-action-required needs delete_repo for two probe repos). Once the identity exists, the acceptance checks apply unchanged.
description: Agents run gh with the owner's token (login joeharris76; scopes admin:org, gist, repo, workflow, write:packages, checked 2026-11-11), and the stand-in attestation check recognises an attester by login only: `consumer.attesters: [joeharris76]` in .github/review.yml (the former STANDIN_ATTESTERS constant in oracle_review_check.py no longer exists), applied by Theseus and by _project/scripts/soundness_merge_digest.py (login in attesters and user_type == "User"). Any agent using the owner's token therefore posts as an attester. Create a GitHub App or fine-grained PAT (or a separate machine user) for agents without admin or workflow scope and not listed in `consumer.attesters`; switch agent gh auth to it; keep stand-in attestation to the human-only identity.
